description: Geography student and GIS intern focused on radar remote sensing. For “Dancing with the SARs” I used NISAR L-band (8 dates, Jul–Oct 2026) to map open water on the Paraguay River floodplain (Corumbá–Ladário to Lake Mandioré) as the river fell, validated it against the Ladário gauge and NASA OPERA DSWx-HLS, and published an open interactive web map. Code and the source of every number: github.com/jpsicilia/spaceapps-2026
summary:
The Paraguay River fell about 1.3 m between July and October 2026. NISAR maps open water reliably, and the river channel and lakes held steady. What declined was partial surface water — pixels only partly covered by water, such as water with emergent vegetation. A simple radar rule misses it; adding InSAR coherence improved detection on one date, but not enough yet.

Using 8 NISAR L-band radar images, we mapped open water on the Pantanal floodplain from Corumbá–Ladário to the Mandioré lagoon and validated it against NASA OPERA optical water maps (DSWx-HLS) and the Ladário river gauge. NISAR maps open water with precision 0.92–1.00. Open water (channel and lagoons) stayed stable; the decline is in partial surface water (DSWx: ≥ 20% and < 100% open water within a 30 m pixel), which tracks the river (r = 0.89, p = 0.008) but is not captured by an L-band open-water rule. An interactive web page shows the change map, hydroperiod and time series, and every number is traceable to its source.
details:
What it does. The project turns NISAR GCOV backscatter (HH and HV) into open-water maps for 8 dates on a 12-day repeat (one 24-day gap, 17 Jul–10 Aug: cycle 026 not available), measures how open water changed, and tests the result against two independent references: OPERA DSWx-HLS (Landsat/Sentinel-2) and the Paraguay River stage at Ladário (ANA station 66825000). Open water is HV < -22 dB and HH < -16 dB (gamma0), adapted from Evans (2013), who reports median L-band σ0 of ≈ −23 dB HH / −30 dB HV for brackish lakes without vegetation (salinas) and ≈ −14 dB HH / −23 dB HV for fresh-water lakes with floating or emergent vegetation (baías); our HH threshold lies between the two classes and our HV threshold is close to the vegetated-lake value.

Results.

  • Open water from NISAR agrees with DSWx-HLS: precision 0.92–1.00, recall 0.65–0.78, IoU 0.62–0.78 (8 pairs).
  • Open water stayed stable (270 → 267 km²); open + partial water declined 1001 → 603 km² and follows the river (r = 0.89, p = 0.008). Partial surface water (DSWx-HLS class 2) is defined as “an inundated area that is at least 20% and less than 100% open water” (OPERA DSWx-HLS Product Specification, JPL D-107395 Rev B, Table 4-1): sub-pixel water such as wetlands, water with emergent vegetation or mixed shoreline pixels. Water depth is not measured.
  • The July→August drop in NISAR open water concentrates on DSWx partial-water pixels (×3.2 vs the plain), which optics still saw wet in August: consistent with vegetation emerging, not with water loss. About a third remains unexplained.
  • Radar vs optical, every date vs most dates: NISAR imaged at least 97.2% of the floodplain on all dates, on a 12-day repeat (one 24-day gap, 17 Jul–10 Aug: cycle 026 not available); optics covered 87–100% on 7 of 8 paired dates, but only 25% on 2 Sep: no HLS/DSWx product exists that day for tile 21KVV, although Sentinel-2B covered the neighbouring tiles.
  • Negative result, reported: a pre-registered classifier could not map partial water from backscatter alone (F1 0.26 (target ≥ 0.50)).

Why it matters. In our study area, partial surface water covered more area than open water in July (DSWx open + partial 1001 km² vs open 270 km²), and it is what an open-water map misses. Knowing what L-band radar does and does not see helps design NISAR-based wetland monitoring.

How we built it. Python (h5py, rasterio, numpy, scipy, scikit-learn, pandas, matplotlib), Leaflet and Chart.js for the web page, GitHub Pages for hosting. Pipeline and order: docs/reproduce.md. Claims register: docs/claims.md.

Use of NASA Data

  • NISAR L2 GCOV (NASA/JPL–ISRO, provisional), track 132 ascending, frame 168, HH and HV, 8 dates, via the ASF DAAC — main data.
  • OPERA DSWx-HLS v1 (PO.DAAC) — independent optical validation (open and partial surface water).
  • NISAR L2 GUNW (NASA/JPL–ISRO, provisional), pair 10→22 Aug 2026, coherence — exploratory test (partial-water F1 0.35 → 0.45). Limitations: labels are DSWx-HLS “partial” (optical, not field data); one pair and one date; coherence depends on temporal baseline and phenology.
